Name: A Little Extra Cheese Please
Author: oclarina
Description:
Have you ever found your Stardew save lacking in the cheese department? This will no longer be a problem.
"A Little Extra Cheese, Please" adds 20 cheese-focused dishes to your recipe repertoire, inspired by real world dishes. All of the dishes are known by default.

Under this spoiler is a list of the ingredients you will need to prepare the dishes in-game:
[spoiler]-27 Cheese
-9 Wheat Flour
-4 Potato
-3 Bread
-3 Corn
-3 Egg (Any)
-2 Hot Pepper
-2 Milk (Any)
-2 Oil
-2 Sugar
-2 Tomato
-1 Common Mushroom
-1 Goat Cheese
-1 Kale
-1 Salmon
-1 Spring Onion
-1 Strawberry
-1 Tortilla[/spoiler]

[size=4][b]List of Dishes[/b][/size]
[size=3][b]Aligot[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 2 Potato, 2 Cheese
Aligot is a French dish made from blended potatoes and cheese. The combination of the starch in the potatoes and the melted cheese (usually a mild variety) give it a signature elastic texture. It's often served alongside other dishes, but the visual of the giant cheese stretch often makes it the main event of a dining experience.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Arepas con Queso[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Corn, 1 Cheese
Arepas are the modern version of an indigenous dish in the regions now known as Colombia and Venezuela, though the dish itself hasn't changed greatly over the years. Corn flour is made into a dough and then grilled. The "con queso" of its name denotes that this variation is stuffed with cheese.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Bagel with Lox and Schmear[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Bread, 1 Cheese, 1 Salmon
An American Jewish dish. Both "Lox" and "Schmear" are loanwords from Yiddish. There's a fine art to preparing each of these ingredients, such that even using the wrong type of water will jeopardize your bagels. You'll probably get a passable result either way, but it really doesn't compare to something made by professionals.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Baked Mac and Cheese[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Wheat Flour, 2 Cheese, 1 Bread
As I know it, Baked Mac and Cheese is a southern cooking staple. There are as many different recipes as there are grandmothers ready to cook it for the holidays, but this specific item was inspired by my own mom's recipe. She always makes a proper roux to melt the cheese in, which she calls her "pot of golden deliciousness," and there's absolute mountains of different types of cheese that she shreds by hand to add into it. Then, just so it doesn't feel quite as indulgent to eat it, she adds in green peas before baking it so at least there's a bit of vegetables in there, though I omitted that part from the Stardew recipe.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Cheese Crunchies[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Corn, 1 Oil
Off-brand legally distinct cheese flavored corn-puff snacks. [s]They're Cheetos. Don't tell anyone.[/s] I heard a rumor once that this sort of snack food was originally a waste product from corn processing, then they realized they could sell it, but I don't know how true that is. There's also a secret hiding for you if you eat them in-game.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Zuzu Style Cheesecake[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Egg (Any), 1 Sugar, 1 Cheese
This is, by far, my favorite type of cake, even if it only bares a scant resemblance to other varieties. Thankfully this is a New York style cheesecake, just rebranded for Stardew, because I tried making a no-bake cheesecake once, and I don't know if I did something wrong, but the end result made it very clear that what I had just made was cream cheese flavored gelatin. It could be user error, but I also think the no-bake kind is just not for me.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Cheesedog[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Cheese, 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Corn
Inspired by a Korean Corndog. The cheese pulls you get from those put traditional mozzarella sticks to shame. Plus, if you get the kind I mimicked here, it eliminates the gross part of corndogs (the hotdog). Maybe I just want to eat cornbread, actually.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Adjaruli Khachapuri[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Egg, 1 Cheese
I tried this Georgian dish on a whim once and fell absolutely in love. I could have it at least once a week and not get bored of it. There's actually different varieties of Khachapuri from different regions of Georgia, but I feel like the Adjaruli version is popular in the US because of the striking visual of the runny egg on top. One day I will try every version, though.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Paneer Tikka[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Cheese, 1 Spring Onion, 1 Hot Pepper, 1 Tomato
Indian cuisine cooked in a Tandoor oven. Prior to making this mod, I had heard of Chicken Tikka, but I didn't know there was a version made with Paneer instead, which is a type of Indian cheese. I've been desperate to try it ever since.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Poutine[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Potato, 1 Common Mushroom, 1 Cheese
A Quebecois, or French Canadian dish, though it's understandably gained popularity outside of Quebec. I used the common mushroom to represent the gravy in the Stardew recipe, since there's no meat, so we can just call this a vegetarian version. Poutine is specifically made with french fried potatoes, cheese curds, and gravy. If you use other cheese it won't be the same.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Provoleta[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 2 Cheese
Provoleta is an Argentinian cheese, which is technically still provoleta even if you don't grill it, I think? But why would you deprive yourself of the extra yumminess added by grilling. It's a sort of firm provolone cheese, so it holds its shape a lot better than other cheeses would by an open flame, allowing it to get char marks like a piece of meat.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Five-Cheese Quesadilla[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 5 Cheese, 2 Flour
This is a dish that I regularly make at home, and I really do use five cheeses, though some of them come pre-shredded and pre-mixed. In essence, a quesadilla is a simple dish with two ingredients, that only requires a flat heated surface to cook, so it's really easy, but I find that by mixing different types of cheeses that have different flavor profiles and reactions to heat, you can get really interesting flavors and texture combinations. I especially like how the cotija doesn't melt like the other cheeses, so you get little pockets of saltier cheese as you eat the quesadilla.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Queso Fundido[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Cheese, 1 Hot Pepper, 1 Tortilla, 1 Oil
Tortilla chips and melted queso blanco are a [i]really[/i] common appetizer at American Mexican and tex-mex restaurants, and without supervision I always end up eating an absolutely irresponsible amount of them. They're very much a "once you start you can't stop" kind of food.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Raclette[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 3 Cheese, 1 Potato
Raclette is a Swiss preparation method for cheese, though it's spread to other nearby countries, probably because it's delicious. The act of scraping the melted parts off an entire half-cheese wheel is an incredible spectacle, and probably worth it for the experience, even if you can get a similar result with a tabletop grill called a raclonette.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Saganaki[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Goat Cheese
Part of Greek Cuisine. Saganaki can technically be anything cooked in the small frying pan it's named after, but a goat or sheep cheese appetizer is the most common.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Sandesh[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Cheese, 1 Sugar, 1 Milk (Any)
A Bengali dessert made of milk and/or chhena or paneer. It can be prepared as simply as tossing the cheese with sugar or flavored and pressed into molds to create complex works of art that are almost too beautiful to eat. I would eat it anyways, though.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Strawberry Blintz Crepes[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Strawberry, 1 Cheese, 1 Wheat Flour
This dish is specifically based on my favorite thing to order at a local restaurant. A blintz is a sort of flat pancake similar to a crepe or a blini that comes from Ashkenazi Jewish cuisine, usually filled with sweetened cheese, and then this one is topped with strawberry preserves. So really, the name "Blintz Crepes" is redundant, but in my defense, I copied it directly from the restaurant's menu.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Tiropita[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Egg (Any), 1 Cheese
A Greek pastry. To be honest, I'm more familiar with spanakopita and baklava, but I would do anything for any dish made with phyllo dough. If you haven't had it before, you definitely should.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]Tomato Grilled Cheese[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Bread, 1 Tomato, 1 Cheese
A grilled cheese sandwich is perfectly fine on its own, or with tomato soup if it [i]must[/i] have an accompaniment. I'd like to have a word with whoever decided to put tomato [i]inside[/i] the sandwich. Get that out of there.
[/spoiler]
[size=3][b]White Sauce Pizza[/b][/size]
[spoiler]
[b]Ingredients:[/b] 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Kale, 1 Milk (Any), 1 Cheese
If you're sensitive to tomatoes for any reason, I really do recommend you try a white sauce pizza. I get them instead of regular frozen pizzas and I've never had any regrets. Except for the fact I'm eating frozen pizza instead of fresh.
[/spoiler]

[b][size=4]Compatibility[/size][/b]
No known incompatibilities. A Little Extra Cheese, Please should work with any other mods that add recipes or alter the cooking process (though it hasn't been rigorously tested). It however, doesn't have context tag-enabled recipes, so you will have to use the vanilla ingredients listed and not any alternatives.
